title: u says /u/
parentNote: u is the fourth of the five vowels, and after today only e is left. It opens more doors than any sound since the first week: up, us, but, run, sun, jump, must, munch. "up" in particular is a word this course has not been able to write down once in thirty-eight days. The trouble with u is that it has the least shape of any vowel — the mouth just drops open and grunts — so a child who is unsure of a middle sound tends to guess a instead, and cup comes out cap. That is exactly what the pairs in the middle of today's lesson are for: cup and cap, hut and hot, bug and big. Say both words slowly yourself and let them hear that only the middle moved.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth flops open and your tongue does nothing at all. It is the grunt in up.
activities.prompt: This is the fourth vowel. After today there is only one left.
Three vowels, all made with your mouth open. Find the one that just grunts.
Same again. Listen for the one with no shape at all.
Only two sounds, and the course has been waiting a long time for this one.
Only the middle sound is new. The rest you have known for weeks.
A blend on the end. Keep the m and the p in one piece.
The longest one. Four sounds, and the last two letters are a team.
Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle.
Same again. Only the vowel moved.

Three this time. Two of them change the middle and one changes the end.

activities.title: The duck on the bus
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: A duck got on the bus and sat on Gus.
Gus did not fuss. Gus did not jump up.
The duck did munch a bun and did honk a lot.
Gus got up and sat at the back.
The duck did jump up and sat on Gus!
